cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Acknowledge the Disrespect
cards.instruction: Make someone apologize for the disrespect to your position, not merely for what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. You told the trainees their head trainer was an idiot. I want an apology.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. For undermining their head trainer. They still need to follow my instructions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll email them after tomorrow's drill.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read it to them before the drill. My whistle isn't going to outrank 'idiot' on its own.

heightening.evidence: B4 timing would leave the next drill under the insult, so A5 requires public repair first.

specificity.evidence: A1 trainees heard idiot, A3 instructions and B4 tomorrow drill establish practical consequences of the position attack.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 whistle-versus-idiot ranking is earned by the need to command the very audience B will address.
